Symptom-rhythm correlation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 76-year-old reports three episodes of unexplained near-syncope over two months. An office ECG shows sinus rhythm at 54/min, but he is asymptomatic during recording. No reversible cause is apparent. Which next step best helps establish whether bradycardia explains his symptoms?

  1. Permanent pacing solely because the rate is below 60/min
  2. Empiric beta-blocker escalation
  3. A single repeat blood pressure measurement
  4. Routine electrical cardioversion
  5. Ambulatory ECG monitoring matched to symptom frequency
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Ambulatory ECG monitoring matched to symptom frequency

Longer monitoring can correlate symptoms with pauses or slowing.

Understanding the options

Ambulatory ECG monitoring matched to symptom frequency
Longer monitoring can correlate symptoms with pauses or slowing.
Permanent pacing solely because the rate is below 60/min
There is no universal rate alone that establishes a pacing indication for sinus-node dysfunction.
Empiric beta-blocker escalation
Additional beta blockade can aggravate slowing.
A single repeat blood pressure measurement
Blood pressure measurement alone cannot establish a rhythm-symptom relationship.
Routine electrical cardioversion
Cardioversion does not evaluate intermittent bradyarrhythmia.
